newsitem.title: CHINA: China shares close higher, but investors back off.
newsitem.headline: China shares close higher, but investors back off.

text.p: China's A and B share indices ended higher on Thursday due to some institutional speculation in selected stocks, but most investors remained sidelined waiting for market-moving news, brokers said.
Shanghai's B index rose 0.293 points or 0.43 percent to 69.019 on volume of 21.1 million shares worth $9.26 million.
Brokers said that although the index breached the 69-point resistance level, follow-up buying was limited.

"Institutional speculation in heavily weighted stocks pushed the index up, but most investors took a wait-and-see attitude, waiting for the release of (companies') 1996 annual reports," said a broker.
Another broker said gains on the A share market encouraged domestic buying on the B share market.

"Recent talk on restructuring state assets in state-owned listed companies and comments in the official media urging unlisted firms that make good profits to consider backdoor listings -- all this gave the market an excuse for some speculation in selected stocks," he said.
Backdoor listing refers to bigger unlisted firms buying stakes in smaller listed companies to gain exposure to the stock market.
Hotel group Shanghai New Asia was the star on speculative buying, rising $0.032 or 7.8 percent to $0.442 on volume of 1.1 million shares.
Shanghai Vacuum and Electron Device was the most traded issue. It gained $0.01 or 4.85 percent to $0.216 on volume of 1.3 million shares.
Shenzhen's B share index rose 0.59 points or 0.38 percent to close at 155.51 on turnover of HK$52.34 million against Wednesday's HK$55.25 million.
Brokers attributed the gains to a strong economic forecast, but added most overseas institutions had put their buy orders on hold as they sit out the annual reporting season.
China on Sunday announced an 8.0 percent gross domestic product growth target and a 6.0 percent goal for retail price inflation for 1997.
On Shenzhen's B share market, appliance maker Tsann Kuen was the best performer, gaining HK$0.08 or 2.09 percent to close at HK$3.90 on volume of 431,700 shares.
Shanghai A shares ended sharply higher, with hot money flowing into stocks expected to be subject to restructuring or selected for backdoor listings, brokers said.
The index jumped 28.876 points or 2.63 percent to 1,128.343 points on volume of 827 million shares worth 7.8 billion yuan.
The SSE30 index closed up 40.633 points or 1.44 percent to 2,860.959 points.
Fujian Fulian was the star on bargain-hunting, surging 0.69 yuan or 10.07 percent to 7.54 yuan on volume of 2.5 million shares.
Shenzhen's A share index gained 4.83 points or 1.23 percent to 396.09 on turnover of 6.22 billion yuan compared with Wednesday's 10.81 billion.
The indefinite suspension of trading in Hainan Minyuan Agricultural Development Co, announced on Wednesday, still weighed on the market, some brokers said.
Authorities are investigating the company for alleged violation of accounting rules in its 1996 annual report.
Others said they expected the effect of the Minyuan news to diminish as investors digested the news.
"Authorities will probably pay more attention to annual reports now the Minyuan event has happened," said Song Bin, an analyst at Central-South Securities.
"But the market mood is still buoyant given last week's strong economic target figures," he said.
Steel products maker Chengdu Lianyi, which listed 24.8 million A shares in Shenzhen on Thursday, ended the day at 14.44 yuan on volume of 11.3 million shares.
